verses.lat: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: lavábis me, et super nivem dealbabor.
verses.eng: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

verses.lat: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
verses.eng: To my hearing Thou shalt give joy and gladness: and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

verses.lat: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
verses.eng: Turn away Thy face from my sins: and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.lat: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: et spíritum rectum ínova in viscéribus meis.
verses.eng: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

verses.lat: Ne projícias me a fácie tua: et Spíritum Sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
verses.eng: Cast me not away from Thy face: and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

verses.lat: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: et spíritu principáli confírma me.
verses.eng: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation: and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

verses.lat: Docébo iníquos vias tuas: et ímpii ad te converténtur.
verses.eng: I will teach the unjust Thy ways: and the wicked shall be converted to Thee.

verses.lat: Líbera me de sangúinibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: Deliver me from blood, O God, Thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol Thy justice.

verses.lat: Dómine, lábia mea apéries: et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
verses.eng: O Lord, Thou wilt open my lips: and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

verses.lat: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: holocáustis non delectáberis.
verses.eng: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: with burnt offerings Thou wilt not be delighted.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribúlátus: cor contrítum et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
verses.eng: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.

verses.lat: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: ut ædificéntur muri Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: Deal favourably, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion: that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

verses.lat: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium justítiæ, oblatiónes et holocáusta: tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
verses.eng: Then shalt Thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations, and whole burnt offerings: then shall they lay calves upon Thy altar.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso érue me.
verses.eng: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

verses.lat: Quia tu es, Deus, fortítudo mea: quare me repulísti? Et quare tristis incédo, dum affígit me inímicus?
verses.eng: For Thou art God, my strength: why hast Thou cast me off? And why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: ipsa me deduxérunt et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
verses.eng: Send forth Thy light and Thy truth: they have conducted me and brought me unto Thy holy hill, and into Thy tabernacles.

verses.lat: Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: ad Deum qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
verses.eng: And I will go in to the altar of God: to God who giveth joy to my youth.

verses.lat: Confitebor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: quare tristis es, ánima mea? Et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: To Thee, O God, my God, I will give praise upon the harp: why art thou sad, O my soul? And why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: Hope in God, for I will still give praise to Him: the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum vadam ad portas ínferi.
verses.eng: I said: In the midst of my days I shall go to the gates of hell.

verses.lat: Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum.
verses.eng: I sought for the residue of my years.

verses.lat: Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, et habitátórem quiétis.
verses.eng: I shall behold man no more, nor the dweller in rest.

verses.lat: Generátio mea abláta est, et convólúta est a me, quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
verses.eng: My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, as a shepherd’s tent.

verses.lat: Præcísa est velut a texénte vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
verses.eng: My life is cut off as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, He cut me off: from morning even to night Thou wilt make an end of me.

verses.lat: Sperábam usque ad mane; quasi leo, sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: I hoped till morning; as a lion, so hath He broken all my bones.

verses.lat: De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: sicut pullus hirúndinis, sic clamábo; meditábor ut colúmba.
verses.eng: From morning even to night Thou wilt make an end of me: I will cry like a young swallow; I will meditate like a dove.

verses.lat: Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, suspiciéntes in excélsum.
verses.eng: My eyes are weakened, looking upward.

verses.lat: Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
verses.eng: Lord, I suffer violence, answer Thou for me. What shall I say, or what shall He answer me, whereas He Himself hath done it?

verses.lat: Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: I will recount to Thee all my years, in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.lat: Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me et vivificábis me.
verses.eng: O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, Thou shalt correct me, and make me to live.

verses.lat: Ecce in pace amaritúdo mea amarissima: tu autem eruísti ánimam meam, ut non períret: projecisti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
verses.eng: Behold, in peace is my bitterness most bitter: but Thou hast delivered my soul, that it should not perish: Thou hast cast all my sins behind Thy back.

verses.lat: Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: For hell shall not confess to Thee, neither shall death praise Thee: nor shall they that go down into the pit look for Thy truth.

verses.lat: Vivens, vivens, ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: The living, the living, he shall give praise to Thee, as I do this day: the father shall make Thy truth known to the children.

verses.lat: Dómine, salvum me fac, et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
verses.eng: O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Ad te levávi óculos meos, qui hábitas in cælis.
verses.eng: To Thee have I lifted up my eyes, who dwellest in heaven.

verses.lat: Ecce sicut óculi servórum in mánibus dominórum suórum,
verses.eng: Behold, as the eyes of servants are on the hands of their masters,

verses.lat: Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: so are our eyes unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.

verses.lat: Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: quia multum repléti sumus despectióne.
verses.eng: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are greatly filled with contempt.

verses.lat: Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: oppóbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
verses.eng: For our soul is greatly filled: we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël:
verses.eng: If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say:

verses.lat: Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos:
verses.eng: If it had not been that the Lord was with us, when men rose up against us:

verses.lat: Forte vivos deglutíssent nos: cum irascéretur furor eórum in nos.
verses.eng: Perhaps they had swallowed us up alive: when their fury was enkindled against us.

verses.lat: Forsítan aqua absorbuísset nos.
verses.eng: Perhaps the waters had swallowed us up.

verses.lat: Torréntem pertránsivit ánima nostra: forsítan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolérábilem.
verses.eng: Our soul hath passed through a torrent: perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus, qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord, who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.

verses.lat: Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est de láqueo venántium:
verses.eng: Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow out of the snare of the fowlers:

verses.lat: Láqueus contrítus est, et nos liberáti sumus.
verses.eng: The snare is broken, and we are delivered.

verses.lat: Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, qui fecit cælum et terram.
verses.eng: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth in Jerusalem.

verses.lat: Montes in circúitu ejus: et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum.
verses.eng: Mountains are round about it: so the Lord is round about His people, from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem justórum: ut non exténdant justi ad iniquitátem manus suas.
verses.eng: For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.

verses.lat: Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, et rectis corde.
verses.eng: Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, and to the upright of heart.

verses.lat: Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: pax super Israël.
verses.eng: But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: peace upon Israel.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion, facti sumus sicut consoláti.
verses.eng: When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, we became like men comforted.

verses.lat: Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: et lingua nostra exsultatióne.
verses.eng: Then was our mouth filled with gladness: and our tongue with joy.

verses.lat: Tunc dicent inter gentes: Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.
verses.eng: Then shall they say among the Gentiles: The Lord hath done great things for them.

verses.lat: Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobiscum: facti sumus lætántes.
verses.eng: The Lord hath done great things for us: we are become joyful.

verses.lat: Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, sicut torrens in Austro.
verses.eng: Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as a stream in the south.

verses.lat: Qui séminant in lácrimis, in exsultatióne metent.
verses.eng: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.

verses.lat: Eúntes ibant et flebant, mitténtes sémina sua.
verses.eng: Going, they went and wept, casting their seeds.

verses.lat: Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, portántes manípulos suos.
verses.eng: But coming, they shall come with joyfulness, carrying their sheaves.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Dixi: Custódiam vias meas, ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
verses.eng: I said: I will take heed to my ways: that I sin not with my tongue.

verses.lat: Pósui ori meo custódiam, cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
verses.eng: I set a guard to my mouth, when the sinner stood against me.

verses.lat: Obmútui et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis, et dolor meus renovátus est.
verses.eng: I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: and my sorrow was renewed.

verses.lat: Concáluit cor meum intra me, et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
verses.eng: My heart grew hot within me: and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.

verses.lat: Locútus sum in lingua mea: Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
verses.eng: I spoke with my tongue: O Lord, make me know my end.

verses.lat: Et númerum diérum meórum quis est, ut sciam quid desit mihi.
verses.eng: And what is the number of my days: that I may know what is wanting to me.

verses.lat: Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos, et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
verses.eng: Behold, Thou hast made my days measurable: and my substance is as nothing before Thee.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, omnis homo vivens.
verses.eng: And indeed all things are vanity: every man living.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo; sed et frustra conturbátur.
verses.eng: Surely man passeth as an image: yea, and he is disquieted in vain.

verses.lat: Thesaurízat, et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
verses.eng: He storeth up: and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.

verses.lat: Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? Et substántia mea apud te est.
verses.eng: And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? And my substance is with Thee.

verses.lat: Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me; oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
verses.eng: Deliver Thou me from all my iniquities: Thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.

verses.lat: Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti.
verses.eng: I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because Thou hast done it.

verses.lat: Amóve a me plagas tuas.
verses.eng: Remove Thy scourges from me.

verses.lat: A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus; propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
verses.eng: The strength of Thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: Thou hast corrected man for iniquity.

verses.lat: Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus; verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
verses.eng: And Thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: surely in vain is any man disquieted.

verses.lat: Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam; áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
verses.eng: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: give ear to my tears.

verses.lat: Ne síleas, quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, sicut omnes patres mei.
verses.eng: Be not silent: for I am a stranger with Thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were.

verses.lat: Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, et ámplius non ero.
verses.eng: O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, and be no more.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, and He was attentive to me.

verses.lat: Et exaudívit preces meas, et edúxit me de lacu misériæ et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: And He heard my prayers, and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: Et státuit super petram pedes meos, et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: And He set my feet upon a rock, and directed my steps.

verses.lat: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: And He put a new canticle into my mouth, a song to our God.

verses.lat: Vidébunt multi et timébunt, et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: Many shall see, and shall fear: and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Beátus vir cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus, et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord, and who hath not had regard to vanities and lying follies.

verses.lat: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine Deus meus, mirabília tua; et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast done many wonderful things, O Lord my God: and in Thy thoughts there is no one like to Thee.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi et locútus sum; multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: I have declared and I have spoken: they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti; aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: Sacrifice and oblation Thou didst not desire: but Thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti; tunc dixi: Ecce vénio.
verses.eng: Burnt offering and sin offering Thou didst not require: then said I: Behold I come.

verses.lat: In cápite libri scriptum est de me, ut fácerem voluntátem tuam; Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do Thy will: O my God, I have desired it, and Thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna; ecce lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: I have declared Thy justice in a great church: lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, Thou knowest it.

verses.lat: Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo; veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: I have not hid Thy justice within my heart: I have declared Thy truth and Thy salvation.

verses.lat: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam a concílio multo.
verses.eng: I have not concealed Thy mercy and Thy truth from a great council.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me; misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: Withhold not Thou, O Lord, Thy tender mercies from me: Thy mercy and Thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala quorum non est númerus; comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: For evils without number have surrounded me: my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me; Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quǽrunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul to take it away.

verses.lat: Convertántur retrórsum et revereántur, qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be turned backward and be ashamed, that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: Let them immediately bear their confusion, that say to me: 'Tis well, 'tis well.

verses.lat: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te, et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus, qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: Let all that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: and let such as love Thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: Ego autem mendícus sum et pauper; Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: But I am a beggar and poor: the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus et protéctor meus tu es; Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: Thou art my helper and my protector: O my God, be not slack.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus, áuribus nostris audívimus; patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
verses.eng: O God, we have heard with our ears: our fathers have declared to us.

verses.lat: Opus quod operátus es in diébus eórum, et in diébus antíquis.
verses.eng: The work Thou hast wrought in their days, and in the days of old.

verses.lat: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos; afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
verses.eng: Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and Thou plantedst them: Thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.

verses.lat: Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos.
verses.eng: For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: neither did their own arm save them.

verses.lat: Sed déxtera tua et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui, quóniam complacuísti in eis.
verses.eng: But Thy right hand and Thy arm, and the light of Thy countenance: because Thou wast pleased with them.

verses.lat: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus, qui mandas salútes Jacob.
verses.eng: Thou art Thyself my King and my God, who commandest the saving of Jacob.

verses.lat: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu, et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
verses.eng: Through Thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: and through Thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

verses.lat: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo, et gládius meus non salvábit me.
verses.eng: For I will not trust in my bow: neither shall my sword save me.

verses.lat: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos, et odiéntes nos confudísti.
verses.eng: But Thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: and hast put them to shame that hate us.

verses.lat: In Deo laudábimur tota die, et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
verses.eng: In God shall we glory all the day long: and in Thy name we will give praise for ever.

verses.lat: Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos, et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
verses.eng: But now Thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: and Thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

verses.lat: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros, et qui odérunt nos diripiébant sibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

verses.lat: Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum, et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
verses.eng: Thou hast given us up like sheep of slaughter: and hast scattered us among the nations.

verses.lat: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio, et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
verses.eng: Thou hast sold Thy people for no price: and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

verses.lat: Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, subsannatiónem et derísum his qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

verses.lat: Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus, commoratiónem cápitis in pópulis.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: a shaking of the head among the people.

verses.lat: Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
verses.eng: All the day long my shame is before me: and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

verses.lat: A voce exprobrántis et obloquéntis, a fácie inimíci et persequéntis.
verses.eng: At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

verses.lat: Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos; nec oblíti sumus te, et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
verses.eng: All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten Thee: and we have not done wickedly in Thy covenant.

verses.lat: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum; et declinésti sémitas nostras a via tua.
verses.eng: And our heart hath not turned back: neither hast Thou turned aside our steps from Thy way.

verses.lat: Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
verses.eng: For Thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: and the shadow of death hath covered us.

verses.lat: Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
verses.eng: If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

verses.lat: Nonne Deus requíret ista? Ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
verses.eng: Shall not God search out these things? For He knoweth the secrets of the heart.

verses.lat: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die; æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
verses.eng: Because for Thy sake we are killed all the day long: we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? Exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
verses.eng: Arise, why sleepest Thou, O Lord? Arise, and cast us not off to the end.

verses.lat: Quare fáciem tuam avértis, oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ et tribulatiónis nostræ?
verses.eng: Why turnest Thou Thy face away, and forgettest our want and our trouble?

verses.lat: Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra; conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
verses.eng: For our soul is humbled down to the dust: our belly cleaveth to the earth.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos, et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
verses.eng: Arise, O Lord, help us and redeem us for Thy name's sake.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum; dico ego ópera mea regi.
verses.eng: My heart hath uttered a good word: I speak my works to the King.

verses.lat: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ velóciter scribéntis.
verses.eng: My tongue is the pen of a scrivener that writeth swiftly.

verses.lat: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis; proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in Thy lips: therefore hath God blessed Thee for ever.

verses.lat: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, potentíssime.
verses.eng: Gird Thy sword upon Thy thigh, O Thou most mighty.

verses.lat: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
verses.eng: With Thy comeliness and Thy beauty set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

verses.lat: Propter veritátem et mansuetúdinem et justítiam; et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
verses.eng: Because of truth and meekness and justice: and Thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

verses.lat: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent, in corda inimicórum regis.
verses.eng: Thy arrows are sharp: under Thee shall people fall, into the hearts of the King's enemies.

verses.lat: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi; virga directiónis, virga regni tui.
verses.eng: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of Thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

verses.lat: Dilexísti justítiam et odísti iniquitátem; proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved justice and hated iniquity: therefore God, Thy God, hath anointed Thee with the oil of gladness above Thy fellows.

verses.lat: Myrrha et gutta et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis; ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
verses.eng: Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume Thy garments, from the ivory houses: out of which the daughters of kings have delighted Thee in Thy glory.

verses.lat: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.
verses.eng: The queen stood on Thy right hand, in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety.

verses.lat: Audi, fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam; et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
verses.eng: Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: and forget thy people and thy father's house.

verses.lat: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum, quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
verses.eng: And the King shall greatly desire thy beauty: for He is the Lord thy God, and Him they shall adore.

verses.lat: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus vultum tuum deprecabúntur; omnes dívites plebis.
verses.eng: And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

verses.lat: Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, in fímbriis áureis, circúmamícta varietátibus.
verses.eng: All the glory of the King's daughter is within, in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

verses.lat: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam; próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
verses.eng: After her shall virgins be brought to the King: her neighbours shall be brought to Thee.

verses.lat: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne; adducéntur in templum Regis.
verses.eng: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: they shall be brought into the temple of the King.

verses.lat: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii; constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
verses.eng: Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

verses.lat: Mémores erunt nóminis tui in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: They shall remember thy name throughout all generations.

verses.lat: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: Therefore shall people praise thee for ever: yea, for ever and ever.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus noster refúgium et virtus; adjútor in tribulatiónibus quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: Our God is our refuge and strength: a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra, et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled, and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: Sonuérunt et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum; conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: Their waters roared and were troubled: the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: the Most High hath sanctified His own tabernacle.

verses.lat: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur; adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna; dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: He uttered His voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum; suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: Veníte et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram.
verses.eng: Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders He hath done upon earth.

verses.lat: Áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ. Arcum cónteret et confrínget arma, et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: Making wars to cease even to the end of the earth. He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield He shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: Vacáte et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus; exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: Be still and see that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum; suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis, in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
verses.eng: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised, in the city of our God, in His holy mountain.

verses.lat: Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, látera aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
verses.eng: With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.

verses.lat: Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur, cum suscípiet eam.
verses.eng: In her houses shall God be known, when He shall protect her.

verses.lat: Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt, convenérunt in unum.
verses.eng: For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: they gathered together.

verses.lat: Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt; tremor apprehéndit eos.
verses.eng: So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: trembling took hold of them.

verses.lat: Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis; in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
verses.eng: There were pains as of a woman in labour: with a vehement wind Thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

verses.lat: Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri; Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
verses.eng: As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God hath founded it for ever.

verses.lat: Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam in médio templi tui.
verses.eng: We have received Thy mercy, O God, in the midst of Thy temple.

verses.lat: Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ; justítia plena est déxtera tua.
verses.eng: According to Thy name, O God, so also is Thy praise unto the ends of the earth: Thy right hand is full of justice.

verses.lat: Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ, propter judícia tua, Dómine.
verses.eng: Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad: because of Thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: Circúmdate Sion et complectímini eam; narráte in túrribus ejus.
verses.eng: Surround Sion, and encompass her: tell ye in her towers.

verses.lat: Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus, et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
verses.eng: Set your hearts on her strength, and distribute her houses, that ye may relate it in another generation.

verses.lat: Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi; ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
verses.eng: For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: He shall rule us for evermore.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Audíte hæc, omnes gentes; áuribus percípite, omnes qui habitátis orbem:
verses.eng: Hear these things, all ye nations: give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

verses.lat: Quique terrígenæ et fílii hóminum, simul in unum dives et pauper.
verses.eng: All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: both rich and poor together.

verses.lat: Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam, et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
verses.eng: My mouth shall speak wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

verses.lat: Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam; apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
verses.eng: I will incline my ear to a parable: I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

verses.lat: Cur timébo in die mala? Iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me.
verses.eng: Why shall I fear in the evil day? The iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

verses.lat: Qui confídunt in virtúte sua, et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
verses.eng: They that trust in their own strength, and glory in the multitude of their riches.

verses.lat: Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo; non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
verses.eng: No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: he shall not give to God his ransom.

verses.lat: Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ; et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
verses.eng: Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

verses.lat: Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes; simul insípiens et stultus períbunt.
verses.eng: He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: the senseless and the fool shall perish together.

verses.lat: Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas; et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
verses.eng: And they shall leave their riches to strangers: and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

verses.lat: Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie; vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
verses.eng: Their dwelling places to all generations: they have called their lands by their names.

verses.lat: Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intéllexit; comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: And man when he was in honour did not understand: he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

verses.lat: Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis, et póstea in ore suo complacebúnt.
verses.eng: This way of theirs is a stumbling-block to them: and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

verses.lat: Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt; mors depáscet eos.
verses.eng: They are laid in hell like sheep: death shall feed upon them.

verses.lat: Et dominabúntur eórum justi in matutíno; et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
verses.eng: And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning: and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi, cum accéperit me.
verses.eng: But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, when He shall receive me.

verses.lat: Ne timúeris cum dives factus fúerit homo, et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus ejus.
verses.eng: Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich: and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

verses.lat: Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia; neque descéndet cum eo glória ejus.
verses.eng: For when he shall die he shall take nothing away: nor shall his glory descend with him.

verses.lat: Quia ánima ejus in vita ipsíus benedicétur; confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
verses.eng: For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: and he will praise Thee when Thou shalt do well to him.

verses.lat: Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum, et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
verses.eng: He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: and he shall never see light.

verses.lat: Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intéllexit; comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: Man when he was in honour did not understand: he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est, et vocávit terram, a solis ortu usque ad occásum.
verses.eng: The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: and He hath called the earth, from the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof.

verses.lat: Ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
verses.eng: Out of Sion the loveliness of His beauty.

verses.lat: Deus maniféste véniet; Deus noster, et non silébit.
verses.eng: God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, and shall not keep silence.

verses.lat: Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet, et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
verses.eng: A fire shall burn before Him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about Him.

verses.lat: Advocábit cælum desúrsum, et terram, discérnere pópulum suum.
verses.eng: He shall call heaven from above, and the earth, to judge His people.

verses.lat: Congregáte illi sanctos ejus, qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
verses.eng: Gather ye together His saints to Him: who set His covenant before sacrifices.

verses.lat: Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus, quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: And the heavens shall declare His justice: for God is judge.

verses.lat: Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar; Israël, et testificábor tibi: Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
verses.eng: Hear, O My people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: I am God, thy God.

verses.lat: Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te; holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
verses.eng: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: and thy burnt offerings are always in My sight.

verses.lat: Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos, neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
verses.eng: I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks.

verses.lat: Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum, juménta in móntibus et boves.
verses.eng: For all the beasts of the woods are Mine: the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

verses.lat: Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli, et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
verses.eng: I know all the fowls of the air: and with Me is the beauty of the field.

verses.lat: Si esuríero, non dicam tibi; meus est enim orbis terræ et plenitúdo ejus.
verses.eng: If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is Mine, and the fulness thereof.

verses.lat: Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum, aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
verses.eng: Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? Or shall I drink the blood of goats?

verses.lat: Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis, et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
verses.eng: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: and pay thy vows to the Most High.

verses.lat: Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis; éruam te, et honorificábis me.
verses.eng: And call upon Me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me.

verses.lat: Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enárras justítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
verses.eng: But to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare My justices, and take My covenant in thy mouth?

verses.lat: Tu vero odísti disciplínam, et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum.
verses.eng: Seeing thou hast hated discipline: and hast cast My words behind thee.

verses.lat: Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo, et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
verses.eng: If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

verses.lat: Os tuum abundávit malítia, et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
verses.eng: Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, and thy tongue framed deceits.

verses.lat: Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum.
verses.eng: Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother's son.

verses.lat: Hæc fecísti, et tácui. Existimásti iníque quod ero tui símilis; árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
verses.eng: These things hast thou done, and I was silent. Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

verses.lat: Intellígite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum; nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
verses.eng: Understand these things, you that forget God: lest He snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me; et illic iter quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
verses.eng: The sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me: and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Quid gloriáris in malítia, qui potens es in iniquitáte?
verses.eng: Why dost thou glory in malice, thou that art mighty in iniquity?

verses.lat: Tota die injustítiam cogitávit lingua tua; sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
verses.eng: All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

verses.lat: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem, iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

verses.lat: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, lingua dolósa.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, O deceitful tongue.

verses.lat: Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem; evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo, et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: He will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

verses.lat: Vidébunt justi et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt et dicent:
verses.eng: The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say:

verses.lat: Ecce homo qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum; sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum, et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
verses.eng: Behold the man that made not God his helper: but trusted in the abundance of his riches: and prevailed in his vanity.

verses.lat: Ego autem sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei; sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, have hoped in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

verses.lat: Confitébor tibi in sǽculum quia fecísti, et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
verses.eng: I will praise Thee for ever, because Thou hast done it: and I will wait on Thy name, for it is good in the sight of Thy saints.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Miserére mei, Deus, secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy.

verses.lat: Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, dele iniquitátem meam.
verses.eng: And according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies blot out my iniquity.

verses.lat: Amplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea, et a peccáto meo munda me.
verses.eng: Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

verses.lat: Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco, et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
verses.eng: For I know my iniquity, and my sin is always before me.

verses.lat: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci; ut justificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
verses.eng: To Thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before Thee: that Thou mayst be justified in Thy words, and mayst overcome when Thou art judged.

verses.lat: Ecce enim in iniquitátibus concéptus sum, et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
verses.eng: For behold I was conceived in iniquities: and in sins did my mother conceive me.

verses.lat: Ecce enim veritátem dilexísti; incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
verses.eng: For behold Thou hast loved truth: the uncertain and hidden things of Thy wisdom Thou hast made manifest to me.

verses.lat: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor; lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
verses.eng: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

verses.lat: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam, et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
verses.eng: To my hearing Thou shalt give joy and gladness: and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

verses.lat: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis, et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
verses.eng: Turn away Thy face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.lat: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
verses.eng: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

verses.lat: Ne projícias me a fácie tua, et Spíritum Sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
verses.eng: Cast me not away from Thy face: and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

verses.lat: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui, et spíritu principáli confírma me.
verses.eng: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation, and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

verses.lat: Docébo iníquos vias tuas, et ímpii ad te converténtur.
verses.eng: I will teach the unjust Thy ways: and the wicked shall be converted to Thee.

verses.lat: Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ, et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: Deliver me from blood, O God, Thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol Thy justice.

verses.lat: Dómine, lábia mea apéries, et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
verses.eng: O Lord, Thou wilt open my lips: and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

verses.lat: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique; holocáustis non delectáberis.
verses.eng: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: with burnt offerings Thou wilt not be delighted.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus; cor contrítum et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
verses.eng: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.

verses.lat: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion, ut ædificéntur muri Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: Deal favourably, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion: that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

verses.lat: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium justítiæ, oblatiónes et holocáusta; tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
verses.eng: Then shalt Thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations, and whole burnt offerings: then shall they lay calves upon Thy altar.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor; a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.
verses.eng: Hear, O God, my prayer when I make supplication to Thee: deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.

verses.lat: Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium, a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.
verses.eng: Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant: from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.

verses.lat: Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas; intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
verses.eng: For they have whetted their tongues like a sword: they have bent their bow a bitter thing, to shoot in secret the undefiled.

verses.lat: Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt; firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.
verses.eng: They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: they are resolute in wickedness.

verses.lat: Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos; dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?
verses.eng: They have talked of hiding snares: they have said: Who shall see them?

verses.lat: Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes; defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.
verses.eng: They have searched after iniquities: they have failed in their search.

verses.lat: Accédet homo ad cor altum, et exaltábitur Deus.
verses.eng: Man shall come to a deep heart: and God shall be exalted.

verses.lat: Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum, et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.
verses.eng: The arrows of children are their wounds: and their tongues against them are made weak.

verses.lat: Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos, et tímuit omnis homo.
verses.eng: All that saw them were troubled: and every man was afraid.

verses.lat: Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, et facta ejus intellexérunt.
verses.eng: And they declared the works of God: and understood His doings.

verses.lat: Lætábitur justus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo; et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.
verses.eng: The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in Him: and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Exsultávit cor meum in Dómino, et exaltátum est cornu meum in Deo meo.
verses.eng: My heart hath rejoiced in the Lord, and my horn is exalted in my God.

verses.lat: Dilatátum est os meum super inimícos meos, quia lætáta sum in salutári tuo.
verses.eng: My mouth is enlarged over my enemies: because I have joyed in Thy salvation.

verses.lat: Non est sanctus ut est Dóminus; neque enim est álius extra te, et non est fortis sicut Deus noster.
verses.eng: There is none holy as the Lord is: for there is no other beside Thee, and there is none strong like our God.

verses.lat: Nolíte multiplicáre loqui sublímia gloriántes; recédant vétera de ore vestro.
verses.eng: Do not multiply to speak lofty things, boasting: let old matters depart from your mouth.

verses.lat: Quia Deus scientiárum Dóminus est, et ipsi præparántur cogitatiónes.
verses.eng: For the Lord is a God of all knowledge, and to Him are thoughts prepared.

verses.lat: Arcus fórtium superátus est, et infírmi accíncti sunt róbore.
verses.eng: The bow of the mighty is overcome, and the weak are girt with strength.

verses.lat: Repléti prius, pro pánibus se locavérunt; et famélici saturáti sunt.
verses.eng: They that were full before have hired out themselves for bread: and the hungry are filled.

verses.lat: Donec stérilis péperit plúrimos, et quæ multos habébat fílios, infirmáta est.
verses.eng: So that the barren hath borne many: and she that had many children is weakened.

verses.lat: Dóminus mortíficat et vivíficat; dedúcit ad ínferos et redúcit.
verses.eng: The Lord killeth and maketh alive: He bringeth down to hell, and bringeth back again.

verses.lat: Dóminus páuperem facit et ditat; humíliat et súblevat.
verses.eng: The Lord maketh poor and maketh rich: He humbleth and He exalteth.

verses.lat: Súscitat de púlvere egénum, et de stércore élevat páuperem, ut sédeat cum princípibus, et sólium glóriæ téneat.
verses.eng: He raiseth up the needy from the dust, and lifteth up the poor from the dunghill: that he may sit with princes, and hold the throne of glory.

verses.lat: Dómini enim sunt cárdines terræ, et pósuit super eos orbem.
verses.eng: For the poles of the earth are the Lord's, and upon them He hath set the world.

verses.lat: Pedes sanctórum suórum servábit, et ímpii in ténebris conticéscent, quia non in fortitúdine sua roborábitur vir.
verses.eng: He will keep the feet of His saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness: because no man shall prevail by his own strength.

verses.lat: Dóminum formidábunt adversárii ejus, et super ipsos in cælis tonábit.
verses.eng: The adversaries of the Lord shall fear Him: and upon them shall He thunder in the heavens.

verses.lat: Dóminus judicábit fines terræ, et dabit impérium regi suo, et sublimábit cornu Christi sui.
verses.eng: The Lord shall judge the ends of the earth, and He shall give empire to His king, and shall exalt the horn of His Christ.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, in vanum laboravérunt qui ǽdificant eam.
verses.eng: Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.

verses.lat: Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
verses.eng: Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

verses.lat: Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere; súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
verses.eng: It is vain for you to rise before light: rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

verses.lat: Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum, ecce heréditas Dómini, fílii; merces, fructus ventris.
verses.eng: When He shall give sleep to His beloved, behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

verses.lat: Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis, ita fílii excussórum.
verses.eng: As arrows in the hand of the mighty, so the children of them that have been shaken.

verses.lat: Beátus vir qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis; non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
verses.eng: Blessed is the man that hath filled his desire from them: he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Beáti omnes qui timent Dóminum, qui ámbulant in viis ejus.
verses.eng: Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: that walk in His ways.

verses.lat: Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis; beátus es, et bene tibi erit.
verses.eng: For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.

verses.lat: Uxor tua sicut vitis abúndans in latéribus domus tuæ.
verses.eng: Thy wife as a fruitful vine on the sides of thy house.

verses.lat: Fílii tui sicut novéllæ olivárum in circúitu mensæ tuæ.
verses.eng: Thy children as olive plants, round about thy table.

verses.lat: Ecce sic benedicétur homo qui timet Dóminum.
verses.eng: Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.

verses.lat: Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion, et vídeas bona Jerúsalem ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ.
verses.eng: May the Lord bless thee out of Sion: and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

verses.lat: Et vídeas fílios filiórum tuórum; pacem super Israël.
verses.eng: And mayst thou see thy children's children: peace upon Israel.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea, dicat nunc Israël.
verses.eng: Often have they fought against me from my youth, let Israel now say.

verses.lat: Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea; étenim non potuérunt mihi.
verses.eng: Often have they fought against me from my youth: but they could not prevail over me.

verses.lat: Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres; prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
verses.eng: The wicked have wrought upon my back: they have lengthened their iniquity.

verses.lat: Dóminus justus concídit cervíces peccatórum.
verses.eng: The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners.

verses.lat: Confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes qui odérunt Sion.
verses.eng: Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.

verses.lat: Fiant sicut fænum tectórum, quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit.
verses.eng: Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: which withereth before it be plucked up.

verses.lat: De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
verses.eng: Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.

verses.lat: Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos; benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
verses.eng: And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine; Dómine, exáudi vocem meam.
verses.eng: Out of the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice.

verses.lat: Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: Let Thy ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine, Dómine, quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: If Thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: Lord, who shall stand it?

verses.lat: Quia apud te propitiátio est; et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
verses.eng: For with Thee there is merciful forgiveness: and by reason of Thy law I have waited for Thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo ejus; sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
verses.eng: My soul hath relied on His word: my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

verses.lat: A custódia matutína usque ad noctem, speret Israël in Dómino.
verses.eng: From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
verses.eng: Because with the Lord there is mercy: and with Him plentiful redemption.

verses.lat: Et ipse rédimet Israël ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
verses.eng: And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Dóminus illuminátio mea et salus mea, quem timébo? Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, a quo trepidábo?
verses.eng: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life, of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.lat: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, ut edant carnes meas: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, ipsi infirmáti sunt et cecidérunt.
verses.eng: Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh: My enemies that trouble me, have themselves been weakened and have fallen.

verses.lat: Si consístant advérsum me castra, non timébit cor meum. Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, in hoc ego sperábo.
verses.eng: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear. If a battle should rise up against me, in this will I be confident.

verses.lat: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram: ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, et vísitem templum ejus.
verses.eng: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. That I may see the delight of the Lord, and may visit His temple.

verses.lat: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
verses.eng: For He hath hidden me in His tabernacle; in the day of evils, He hath protected me in the secret place of His tabernacle.

verses.lat: In petra exaltávit me: et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos. Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
verses.eng: He hath exalted me upon a rock: and now He hath lifted up my head above my enemies. I have gone round, and have offered up in His tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: miserére mei, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to Thee: have mercy on me, and hear me.

verses.lat: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
verses.eng: My heart hath said to Thee: My face hath sought Thee: Thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

verses.lat: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: ne declínes in ira a servo tuo. Adjútor meus esto: ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
verses.eng: Turn not away Thy face from me; decline not in Thy wrath from Thy servant. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not; do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

verses.lat: Quóniam pater meus et mater mea dereliquérunt me: Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
verses.eng: For my father and my mother have left me: but the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.lat: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
verses.eng: Set me, O Lord, a law in Thy way, and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

verses.lat: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
verses.eng: Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; for unjust witnesses have risen up against me, and iniquity hath lied to itself.

verses.lat: Credo vidére bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
verses.eng: Expect the Lord, do manfully: and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
verses.eng: Unto Thee will I cry, O Lord: O my God, be not Thou silent to me: lest if Thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

verses.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
verses.eng: Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to Thee; when I lift up my hands to Thy holy temple.

verses.lat: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, mala autem in córdibus eórum.
verses.eng: Draw me not away together with the wicked; and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not: Who speak peace with their neighbour, but evils are in their hearts.

verses.lat: Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum. Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
verses.eng: Give them according to their works, and according to the wickedness of their inventions. According to the works of their hands give Thou to them: render to them their reward.

verses.lat: Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum ejus: déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
verses.eng: Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of His hands: Thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus: quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord, for He hath heard the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: Dóminus adjútor meus, et protéctor meus: in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adjútus sum. Et reflóruit caro mea: et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
verses.eng: The Lord is my helper and my protector: in Him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped. And my flesh hath flourished again: and with my will I will give praise to Him.

verses.lat: Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: et protéctor salvatiónum christi sui est.
verses.eng: The Lord is the strength of His people, and the protector of the salvation of His anointed.

verses.lat: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
verses.eng: Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thy inheritance: and rule them, and exalt them for ever.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me: nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
verses.eng: I will extol Thee, O Lord, for Thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.

verses.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, clamávi ad te, et sanásti me.
verses.eng: O Lord my God, I have cried to Thee, and Thou hast healed me.

verses.lat: Dómine, eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam: salvásti me a descendéntibus in lacum.
verses.eng: Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: Thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.

verses.lat: Psállite Dómino, sancti ejus: et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
verses.eng: Sing to the Lord, O ye His saints: and give praise to the memory of His holiness.

verses.lat: Quóniam ira in indignatióne ejus: et vita in voluntáte ejus. Ad vésperam demorábitur fletus: et ad matutínum lætítia.
verses.eng: For wrath is in His indignation; and life in His good will. In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.

verses.lat: Ego autem dixi in abundántia mea: Non movébor in ætérnum.
verses.eng: And in my abundance I said: I shall never be moved.

verses.lat: Dómine, in voluntáte tua, præstitísti decóri meo virtútem. Avertísti fáciem tuam a me, et factus sum conturbátus.
verses.eng: O Lord, in Thy favour, Thou gavest strength to my beauty. Thou turnedst away Thy face from me, and I became troubled.

verses.lat: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo: et ad Deum meum deprecábor.
verses.eng: To Thee, O Lord, will I cry: and I will make supplication to my God.

verses.lat: Quæ utílitas in sánguine meo, dum descéndo in corruptiónem? Numquid confitébitur tibi pulvis, aut annuntiábit veritátem tuam?
verses.eng: What profit is there in my blood, whilst I go down to corruption? Shall dust confess to Thee, or declare Thy truth?

verses.lat: Audívit Dóminus, et misértus est mei: Dóminus factus est adjútor meus.
verses.eng: The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: the Lord became my helper.

verses.lat: Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi: conscidísti saccum meum, et circumdedísti me lætítia:
verses.eng: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: Thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:

verses.lat: Ut cantet tibi glória mea, et non compúngar: Dómine, Deus meus, in ætérnum confitébor tibi.
verses.eng: To the end that my glory may sing to Thee, and I may not regret: O Lord my God, I will give praise to Thee for ever.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: in justítia tua líbera me.
verses.eng: In Thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: deliver me in Thy justice.

verses.lat: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, accélera ut éruas me. Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii, ut salvum me fácias.
verses.eng: Bow down Thy ear to me: make haste to deliver me. Be Thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, to save me.

verses.lat: Quóniam fortitúdo mea et refúgium meum es tu: et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
verses.eng: For Thou art my strength and my refuge; and for Thy name's sake Thou wilt lead me and nourish me.

verses.lat: Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
verses.eng: Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: for Thou art my protector.

verses.lat: In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
verses.eng: Into Thy hands I commend my spirit: Thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

verses.lat: Odísti observántes vanitátes supervácue. Ego autem in Dómino sperávi:
verses.eng: Thou hast hated them that regard vanities to no purpose. But I have hoped in the Lord:

verses.lat: Exsultábo et lætábor in misericórdia tua. Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
verses.eng: I will be glad and rejoice in Thy mercy. For Thou hast regarded my humility, Thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

verses.lat: Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
verses.eng: And Thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: Thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

verses.lat: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus.
verses.eng: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly.

verses.lat: Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: et anni mei in gemítibus. Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
verses.eng: For my life is wasted with grief: and my years in sighs. My strength is weakened through poverty: and my bones are disturbed.

verses.lat: Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: et timor notis meis. Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me.
verses.eng: I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours: and a fear to my acquaintance. They that saw me without fled from me.

verses.lat: Oblívioni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde. Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum:
verses.eng: I am forgotten as one dead from the heart. I am become as a vessel that is destroyed.

verses.lat: Quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu: in eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
verses.eng: For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about: while they assembled together against me, they consulted to take away my life.

verses.lat: Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
verses.eng: But I have put my trust in Thee, O Lord: I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in Thy hands.

verses.lat: Eripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, et a persequéntibus me.
verses.eng: Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; and from them that persecute me.

verses.lat: Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
verses.eng: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant; save me in Thy mercy. Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon Thee.

verses.lat: Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: muta fiant lábia dolósa.
verses.eng: Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

verses.lat: Quæ loquúntur advérsus justum iniquitátem: in supérbia, et in abusióne.
verses.eng: Which speak iniquity against the just, with pride and abuse.

verses.lat: Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, quam abscondísti timéntibus te! Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
verses.eng: O how great is the multitude of Thy sweetness, O Lord, which Thou hast hidden for them that fear Thee! Which Thou hast wrought for them that hope in Thee, in the sight of the sons of men.

verses.lat: Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ a conturbatióne hóminum. Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo a contradictióne linguárum.
verses.eng: Thou shalt hide them in the secret of Thy face, from the disturbance of men. Thou shalt protect them in Thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus: quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord, for He hath shown His wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

verses.lat: Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: Projéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum. Ideo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, dum clamárem ad te.
verses.eng: But I said in the excess of my mind: I am cast away from before Thy eyes. Therefore Thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, when I cried to Thee.

verses.lat: Dilígite Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
verses.eng: O love the Lord, all ye His saints: for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

verses.lat: Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, omnes qui sperátis in Dómino.
verses.eng: Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all ye that hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, expúgna impugnántes me.
verses.eng: Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: overthrow them that fight against me.

verses.lat: Apprehénde arma et scutum: et exsúrge in adjutórium mihi.
verses.eng: Take hold of arms and shield: and rise up to help me.

verses.lat: Effúnde frámeam, et conclúde advérsus eos qui persequúntur me: dic ánimæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.
verses.eng: Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: say to my soul: I am thy salvation.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur, quæréntes ánimam meam. Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur cogitántes mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed that seek after my soul. Let them be turned back and be confounded that devise evil against me.

verses.lat: Fiant tamquam pulvis ante fáciem venti: et Ángelus Dómini coárctans eos.
